niches_top.name: Fish otolith (ear-stone) image & chemistry archives
niches_top.score_justification: Raw images + chemistry, dozens of lab collections, reader-vs-reader age gap, known-age anchors exist.

fidelity_card.RAW: High-resolution otolith photographs and LA-ICP-MS / isotope transect files on lab and institute sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fish specimen — hundreds per collection, dozens of species, same imaging protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read by reader A vs reader B vs chemistry; usually only published means survive
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age hatchery fish and bomb-radiocarbon validated ages

niches_top.headline_shape: A stone inside a fish's head has recorded every winter of its life — and two experts reading it can disagree by years.
niches_top.why_niche: Age labs keep their own image piles; there is no central reconciliation product, only per-lab atlases (AFORO, national collections) that never joined each other's readings.

niches_top.name: Weakly electric fish EOD waveform recordings
niches_top.score_justification: Raw .wav is the specimen; species-specific signal; taxonomy rewritten by DNA after recordings were filed by ear.

fidelity_card.RAW: Uncompressed .wav/.mp3 electric-organ-discharge recordings with oscillogram exports, on lab and personal research sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One recorded fish — hundreds of individuals, dozens of species per expedition, one electrode protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species named by waveform at capture vs later DNA-barcode revisions of the same vouchers
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Museum voucher specimens tied to recording numbers

niches_top.headline_shape: A fish that 'sees' with electricity broadcasts its own name in a waveform — and the recordings were filed under names DNA later changed.
niches_top.why_niche: A handful of labs (Cornell mormyrids, Crampton's gymnotiforms) hold expedition piles on their own sites; no cross-lab EOD library exists.

niches_top.name: Frog & toad call archives (regional fonotecas)
niches_top.score_justification: The task's own example: raw .wav/.mp3 per species, regional sound libraries, call IDs vs DNA-split species.

fidelity_card.RAW: Original .wav/.mp3 advertisement-call recordings with accession numbers, on regional fonoteca and lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One calling male — thousands of accessions per fonoteca, hundreds of species, standard field-recorder protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Call filed under the species name at recording vs the DNA-split taxonomy of today (second ruler)

niches_top.headline_shape: A frog smaller than your thumbnail has a unique voice — and thousands of taped voices are filed under species that have since been split in three.
niches_top.why_niche: Fonoteca Zoológica (Madrid), Fonoteca Neotropical and university piles each hold their own accessions; the big platforms host photos, not these accessioned raw calls.

niches_top.name: Salmon & fish scale image archives
niches_top.score_justification: A century of scale envelopes; images are raw growth records; reader ages vs known-tag fish is a clean two-rulers setup.

fidelity_card.RAW: Scale images (slides / scans) plus envelope metadata, held by fisheries labs, rivers trusts and agency image labs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One scale — thousands per river system per decade, one mounting and imaging protocol per lab
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read from the scale vs known age of PIT-tagged / coded-wire-tagged fish (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Tag-recovery fish of exactly known age

niches_top.headline_shape: A salmon carries its whole childhood — river years and ocean years — written in rings on a scale the size of a fingernail.
niches_top.why_niche: Every fisheries lab keeps its own scale library; the 2025 known-age validation set (254 fish) showed how rarely the big archives are ever checked against truth.

niches_top.name: Longitudinal child growth study records
niches_top.score_justification: Same child measured yearly for decades — the rarest design in human biology; most collections joined one consortium, the strays did not.

fidelity_card.RAW: Serial radiographs, photographs, casts and measurement sheets per child, on growth-centre and foundation sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One child — hundreds per study, measured at fixed ages under one protocol for 20+ years
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Skeletal-maturity stage called by rater A vs rater B on the same films (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The child's known chronological age and the Greulich–Pyle / Tanner–Whitehouse atlases built from these very films

niches_top.headline_shape: The same child, X-rayed every birthday from 2 to 25, is a ruler for human growing that no snapshot study can replace.
niches_top.why_niche: Nine US craniofacial collections were consolidated by the AAOF — but the non-craniofacial series, the non-US studies and the two un-joined collections remain on centre sites, un-reconciled.

niches_top.name: Hospital autopsy & cause-of-death ledgers (pre-1950)
niches_top.score_justification: One hospital's dead, protocolled for 70 years; period diagnoses vs modern recoding is a textbook second ruler.
keywords: cause of death register digitised pdf

fidelity_card.RAW: Autopsy protocol books, dissection registers and death registers as PDFs/images on hospital, university and state archive sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One hospital — thousands of protocols per institution, one protocol form for decades
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Diagnosis written at death vs the same case recoded to modern ICD by historians (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The hospitals' own published annual reports and Registrar-General series

niches_top.headline_shape: A hospital's dead, counted the same way for 70 years, show diseases disappearing before the drugs that cured them were invented.
niches_top.why_niche: Each archive digitised its own registers (Barts, Columbia, state asylums) as catalogue PDFs; nobody has built the cross-hospital case-level panel.

niches_top.name: River gauge recorder charts & staff-gauge ledgers
niches_top.score_justification: Rivers wrote their own diaries in ink for a century; chart archives sit in basin agencies, mostly unscanned or singly rescued.

fidelity_card.RAW: Autographic recorder charts and staff-gauge ledger scans on basin-authority, archive and data-rescue project sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One gauge station — hundreds of stations per country, weekly charts for decades, one recorder family
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Level read off the chart vs discharge computed from the period rating curve (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Modern gauging stations and surveyed gauge-zero benchmarks

niches_top.headline_shape: A river wrote down its own height, in ink, every hour for fifty years — most of those diaries have never been read by a computer.
niches_top.why_niche: Data rescue is project-by-project (Bavarian Danube 1826–94 was only rescued in 2025); each basin authority holds its own chart rooms and few series are public.

niches_top.name: Long-term crop experiment plot books (beyond the flagships)
niches_top.score_justification: Same plots, same treatments, a century of yields; the flagship (Rothamsted/Morrow) got curated — the other stations' plot books did not.
keywords: long term agricultural experiment plot data
field trial plot book historical pdf

fidelity_card.RAW: Plot books and yield tables (plot × treatment × year) in experiment-station reports and university archive PDFs
fidelity_card.UNIT: One plot — dozens of stations worldwide, each running one fixed layout for 50–150 years
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Yield printed in the station's annual report vs the plot book's own figure (second ruler)
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: The curated flagship datasets (Rothamsted eRA, Morrow Plots 2022) as method and benchmark

niches_top.headline_shape: The same field, planted the same way since 1876, is an experiment nobody alive will see the end of — and most stations' plot books were never turned into data.
niches_top.why_niche: Morrow Plots were only curated into a dataset in 2022 and Rothamsted has its own archive; the dozens of other long-term stations (Sanborn, Askov, Halle…) publish reports, not plot-level panels.
